title: The counit-defined diagonal comparison in a base-change cube
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. All schemes in this statement are separated and of finite type over $k$, and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the ordinary uncompleted constant-coefficient pro-etale module derived categories and their bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Pullbacks and tensor products are the ordinary derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-tensor].

Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], let $v:Y'\to Y$ be arbitrary, and put $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ with projections $u:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ [def-pc-base-change].
Put $R=\mathbf Z/\ell^r$, $r\ge1$, and use the constructible adjunctions $F_h=Rh_{!,R}\dashv G_h=h_R^!$ [def-pur-co-smoothness]. For each Cartesian square with smooth vertical arrow $h$, define its exceptional exchange as the adjoint transpose of the pulled-back counit composed with inverse compact-support exchange [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate, def-exchange-projection]. Write $\omega_h=G_hR_{\operatorname{cod}(h)}$. Put $W=X\times_Y X$, with projections $p_1,p_2$ and diagonal $\Delta$, and put $W'=X'\times_{Y'}X'$, with projections $p'_1,p'_2$, diagonal $\Delta'$ and induced $q:W'\to W$. Write
$$b_f:p_2^*\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{p_1},\quad b_{f'}:p_2'^*\omega_{f'}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{p'_1},\quad b_{p_1}:q^*\omega_{p_1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{p'_1},\quad e_1:u^*\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{f'}$$
for these specified exchanges. The section invariant is $C(h,s)=s^*\omega_h$ [def-pur-section-invariant]. Define $\kappa_f=\Delta^*b_f^{-1}:C(p_1,\Delta)\to\omega_f$ using $p_2\Delta=1$, and similarly $\kappa_{f'}$, with the canonical pullback composition and identity isomorphisms [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

The pair $(W',p_1',\Delta')$ is canonically the pullback of $(W,p_1,\Delta)$ along $u$; both projections are smooth of pure relative dimension $d$, and the diagonals are regular closed sections of codimension $d$. Every constructible finite-Tor object used in these comparisons has an etale-origin representative on which the compact-support exchanges are the witnessed exchanges of [fix-lem-exchanges], using the explicit transport construction [def-pur-compact-exchange-witness-transport]. Under canonical pullback compositors the following equalities hold in the derived categories:
$$b_{p_1}\circ q^*b_f=b_{f'}\circ p_2'^*e_1,$$
$$\kappa_{f'}\circ\Delta'^*b_{p_1}=e_1\circ u^*\kappa_f.$$
They include identity base change and relative dimension zero, and require no flatness of $v$.

proof.text: The fibre-product universal property identifies $W'$ with $W\times_{X,p_1}X'$. Explicitly, on maps from any scheme $T$, an element of the latter is $((x_1,x_2),(x_1,y'))$ with $f(x_1)=f(x_2)=v(y')$; it corresponds to $((x_1,y'),(x_2,y'))\in W'(T)$. These assignments are inverse and natural in $T$. They carry $p'_1$ to the projection to $X'$ and $q$ to the projection to $W$. They carry $\Delta'$ to the pulled-back section: $q\Delta'=\Delta u$. They also give $p_2q=up'_2$ and $p'_2\Delta'=1$. Thus this is an identification of the pairs with their specified sections, without a flatness assumption.

proof.text: Smooth relative dimension, separatedness and quasi-compact finite type persist under the three pullbacks. Use the proved source-library isRegularImmersion_diagonal at positive dimension; its affine weakly regular generators are a proper regular sequence at points of the diagonal because their ideal is the kernel and its zero locus contains that point. At dimension zero the morphism is etale, its diagonal is open and closed, and on an affine open inside its image the ideal is zero and the empty sequence is regular. This proves the exact affine-local IsRegularOfPureCodimension predicate of PurityConventions for both diagonals.

proof.text: Finite type over the given field gives Noetherian schemes and Nagata compactifications. The prime ell is nonzero in the characteristic-p field, so ell^r is invertible on every scheme in the diagram, including empty schemes. Apply the proved source smooth exceptional-base-change isomorphism to the four squares and specialize to the coefficient unit. For each intrinsic fixed-module constructible input, its finite stratification and fixed lisse pieces give finite models, hence constructible etale-origin cohomology sheaves. The source boundedConstructible_of_homology theorem assembles the bounded etale-origin complex. Its bounded-below witness makes the raw pro-etale compact-support exchange invertible by the source finite-coefficient base-change theorem, and compactSupport_exchange_transport identifies its specified transport with that same raw map. This works directly for ULift(ZMod(ell^r)); no coefficient-extension-ring identification is needed.

proof.text: Use affineLinearExchange_paste for the ordinary etale compact-support exchange maps. Cancel the pullback compositors to express the outer exchange as the composite of the two successive exchanges. Take inverse isomorphisms. The corresponding TwoSquare is the horizontal composite of the inverse squares whiskered by the upper and lower compositors. Apply mateEquiv_whiskerTop_whiskerBottom and mateEquiv_vcomp for the specified rightDerivedUpperShriekAdjunctions. By definition their mates are rightDerivedUpperShriekBaseChangeMap. This proves the full exceptional pasting formula at an arbitrary object.

proof.text: Specialize exceptional pasting at the coefficient unit. Naturality of the second exceptional exchange and the unit clause of canonicalDerivedPullbackCompositionMonoidal combine the unit comparisons into the outer unit comparison, giving dualizingComplexBaseChangeMap pasting. Apply it first to f followed by u and then to v followed by f-prime. The two outer maps are identified by the second projection square and pullback.condition; proof irrelevance identifies the pullback-square witnesses. Cancel the common first compositor. The result is precisely the first displayed diagonalCubePullbackIso equation, and applying comparison inverse image gives its stated pro-etale image.

proof.text: Pull the first equation back along the primed diagonal and use naturality of diagonalCubePullbackIso at b_f. Cancel the adjacent pullbacks of b_f-prime and its inverse, and use naturality of the section compositor at e_1. The proved source leftDerivedUpperStar_map_comp_compSectionIso identifies the remaining section/pullback-compositor chain with the inverse diagonalCubePullbackIso followed by the pulled-back section compositor. Changing its common composite morphism is proved by equality elimination. Cancel this inverse compositor and the pullbacks of b_f and its inverse. This gives exactly the second equation with both kappas expanded as in the original statement; finally apply comparison inverse image. No positivity or flatness is used.
